brief: A single hex base, nothing else added beside or on top of it, with five drawers in it.

requirements.requirement: Single hex base, nothing else added beside or on top of it
requirements.evidence: Build is piece:0,0,0;half-n only, no neighbours on any side or level 1 – the closest the system allows to a single base while still permitting a drawer (full hex permits zero drawers). No other cells occupied.

Configurator allows at most one drawer per half-base (on its cut face, socket s14/s15, drawer:0#0,0#cut). Full, quarter and half bases were all tested – full gives 0 drawer sockets, quarter gives 0, half gives 1 and reports no further drawer sockets. Five drawers in one cell is not offered and cannot be forced via raw ops; placing one fills the only drawer site.

finish.summary: Single half-n base placed with its maximum of one drawer (drawer:0#0,0#cut). Verified in configurator: full base offers 0 drawers, half base offers 1, quarter offers 0, and after placing one drawer no further drawer sockets exist. Five drawers in a single hex cell is not supported by the placement rules, so the built maximum is demonstrated and the five-drawer requirement is marked unmet.

lines.label: M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
